title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page proves Lucas's theorem on binomial coefficients mod p. It serves as a lemma for the divided-power de Rham complex, where products of divided powers involve binomial coefficients: x^[i] x^[j] = c_{ij} x^[i+j].

Notation: c_{ij} = (i+j)!/(i! j!). Write i = sum u_ε p^ε and j = sum v_ε p^ε in base p.

Lemma 1 states two things:
- c_{ij} ≢ 0 mod p if and only if u_ε + v_ε ≤ p−1 for every ε, i.e. there are no carries when adding i and j in base p (Kummer).
- In all cases c_{ij} ≡ ∏ c_{u_ε,v_ε} mod p.

Proof by one-digit induction. Write i = u + pr and j = v + ps with 0 ≤ u, v ≤ p−1. The claim (*) is c_{ij} ≡ c_{u,v} c_{r,s} mod p. To see it, expand (X+Y)^{i+j} in F_p[X,Y] using the Frobenius identity (X+Y)^p = X^p + Y^p. Set t = r+s and w = u+v.

Case w ≤ p−1:
- (X+Y)^{i+j} = (X^p+Y^p)^t (X+Y)^w = Σ C(w,α) C(t,β) X^{α+pβ} Y^{(w−α)+p(t−β)}.
- Since α ≤ w ≤ p−1, uniqueness of base-p digits makes the monomials pairwise distinct.
- The coefficient of X^i Y^j therefore comes from α = u, β = r, giving c_{ij} ≡ C(w,u) C(t,r) = c_{u,v} c_{r,s}.
- Here c_{u,v} ≢ 0 because (u+v)! with u+v < p has no factor p.

Case w ≥ p:
- Write w = p + w' with 0 ≤ w' ≤ p−2, so (X+Y)^{i+j} = (X^p+Y^p)^{t+1} (X+Y)^{w'}.
- A term X^i Y^j would need α = u ≤ w' = u+v−p, i.e. v ≥ p, which is impossible.
- Hence c_{ij} ≡ 0. Specialising to (i,j) = (u,v) gives c_{u,v} ≡ 0, so the product formula still holds.

The next page completes the induction and derives Corollary 2, which evaluates c_{N+1,p^ε−1} and c_{N,p^ε} mod p for N ≡ −1 mod p. These feed Lemma 2, on families x_i with binomial-weighted equalities, which bears on divided-power or de Rham cohomology computations.
errors: No substantive errors; the argument is correct and complete.
Notational slip: in the case w ≥ p the summation bound t' is used without being defined; it should be t' = t+1.
On the next page, the induction is said to be on the length of the expansions 'of u and v'; it should be of i and j.
Minor: in the lemma statement the expansions are indexed up to ν (written 'e' in places).

ideas.what: Multiplicativity of binomial coefficients mod p over base-p digits, and the non-vanishing criterion (no carries)
Proof via the Frobenius identity (X+Y)^p = X^p+Y^p in F_p[X,Y] together with uniqueness of base-p digits
ideas.modern_name: Standard generating-function proof of Lucas's theorem

deep.surprise_reason: This is a textbook proof of Lucas's and Kummer's theorems, written out as a technical lemma for divided-power computations. Nothing new.
transcription_corrections: The sum in the case w ≥ p runs over 0 ≤ β ≤ t' with t' = t+1; the 'ω' in the image is w'.
'2 à 2 [?] ont exposant distinct' likely reads 'sont 2 à 2 d'exposant distinct' (pairwise distinct exponents).
'ce qui n'est pas [?]' should read roughly 'ce qui n'est pas [le cas]', i.e. v ≥ p is impossible since v ≤ p−1.
